name: Storm-1674
iocPatterns: Hidden span tags in Active Directory/Teams tools
Automated queries via MailSniper for target discovery
Offshore and high-risk domain registration patterns
keyCapabilities: Initial Access Brokerage for ransomware groups
Active Directory and Group Policy manipulation
Cloud infrastructure harvesting via Graph API
Automatic data scraping from collaboration suites
Evasion of security software via masquerading
recommendedActions: Block the execution of applications utilizing the 'ms-appinstaller' protocol.
Disable external message reception from untrusted tenants on Microsoft Teams.
Implement alerts for telemetry indicating 'AADInternals' or 'GraphRunner' usage.
Audit Active Directory logs for modifications to the SID-History attribute.
Monitor network traffic for communication via Brute Ratel C4 (BRc4) protocols.
Scan and audit all LNK files for IconEnvironmentDataBlock content.
Implement conditional access policies strictly for M365 and SharePoint logins.
Deploy detection rules for the DarkGate and Pikabot malware families.
campaignsText: Storm-1674 operates with a high operational tempo, frequently collaborating with other cybercrime entities like Sangria Tempest and Storm-1113 to share infrastructure. In late 2023 and early 2024, the group was actively observed in campaigns involving the 'VEILdrive' operations where they used compromised accounts to masquerade as IT support staff on Microsoft Teams. Their tactic of using TeamFiltration to extract contact lists from OneDrive/SharePoint suggests a strategy aimed at wide-scale lateral movement discovery before selling access. The transition from their standard malware delivery (DarkGate) to the deployment of Black Basta indicates a structured, professional pipeline for ransomware preparation.
description: Storm-1674 is a sophisticated Initial Access Broker (IAB) that utilizes social engineering through Microsoft Teams to distribute malware and sell access to ransomware affiliates. The actor is heavily linked to the distribution of DarkGate and the eventual deployment of Black Basta ransomware.
goals: Storm-1674's primary goal is financial gain through the sale of stolen credentials and access to specialized ransomware groups. They target high-value sectors including financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, infrastructure, and government agencies across various geographies, specifically targeting organizations with large footprints in Microsoft 365 environments.
